Session Chair's Sheet — Room 2B, Thursday morning

One room, one projector, one lapel pack, one AV desk, one chair. Three talks, thirty minutes each, with questions after every one. The chair calls each speaker to the lectern; nothing starts until they do.

Before the room opens
Line check at the AV desk: laptop, HDMI, house sound, record feed. 30 minutes.
Test the projector once the desk is up: resolution, keystone, the cue slide. 15 minutes.
Check the lapel pack after the projector: battery, gain, a walk to the back row. 10 minutes.

Slides
Load the first deck once the lapel pack is checked; 10 minutes, and leave it on the cue slide.
Load the second deck as soon as the first talk's questions are over; 5 minutes.
Load the third deck while the coffee is going out; 5 minutes.

The session
Chair opens the room, housekeeping and fire exits; 5 minutes.
First talk when the chair calls the first speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the first talk: five to ten minutes, seven is the plan.
Changeover to the second speaker: unclip the pack, clip it on, 5 minutes.
Second talk when the chair calls the second speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the second talk: five to ten minutes, seven is the plan.
Changeover to the third speaker once the coffee is cleared from the foyer; 5 minutes.
Third talk when the chair calls the third speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the third talk: five to fifteen minutes, ten is the plan.
Chair closes the session; 5 minutes.

Catering
Set the coffee station in the service corridor from ninety minutes in; 30 minutes.
Coffee goes out to the foyer when the second talk's questions end; 20 minutes.
Clear the foyer; 10 minutes.

Strike
Strike the AV desk when the chair closes; 20 minutes, cables coiled, record feed off.

Notes
The projector is the contended thing, not the room: a deck cannot be loaded while a talk is on it, so every load sits in a gap. The lapel pack is the other one, and it is the reason changeovers are real steps rather than slack. Question time is the only elastic in the morning; if the first two run long the chair trims the third.

<<<
Product Launch Evening: Run of Show

Venue: the main hall, 200 seats, one stage with a single projector and a two-microphone PA, and a foyer with a bar. Crew: one producer calling the show, one AV technician, two front-of-house staff and the caterers. Crew call is 5:00 pm, doors are scheduled for 6:00 pm, and the program must be over by 8:00 pm so the reception can run before the venue resets at 9:00 pm.

Pre-show
The AV technician runs a full line check of the projector, clicker and both microphones; allow 30 minutes. The producer then walks the CEO and the product lead through the stage for a 20-minute rehearsal of the keynote transitions. Meanwhile front-of-house sets up the registration desk and lays out name badges, which takes 45 minutes, then does a 15-minute walkthrough of the foyer and the seating. Catering sets the bar and the canapé stations in the foyer over 60 minutes.

Doors
Doors open on the producer's call, not before front-of-house confirms the walkthrough is done. Guests arrive and register over 30 minutes while a welcome playlist runs in the hall and the bar serves drinks. When registration closes, front-of-house ushers guests to their seats, which takes 5 minutes.

Program
The host opens the program as soon as the hall is seated and welcomes the audience for 5 minutes. The CEO keynote begins on the host's cue and runs 20 minutes; the AV technician brings up the deck. Straight after the keynote the technician plays a 2-minute product video from the booth, and the product lead follows with a 25-minute live demo. A moderated Q&A follows for about 20 minutes, no less than 15 and no more than 25; the moderator closes it when the questions run dry or the clock says so. When the moderator hands back, the host closes the program in 5 minutes and invites everyone to the reception.

Reception
The foyer bar reopens as soon as the host closes, and catering circulates canapés for 45 minutes. Front-of-house breaks down the registration desk once the last guests have left the hall, about 15 minutes, and the AV technician strikes the stage over 30 minutes after the hall is clear.
>>>

<<<
Load-In Schedule — The Lyric, one-nighter

One loading dock, one stage, one lighting desk, one PA, one monitor world. Crew call is 8am and that is where this schedule starts. The dock takes one truck at a time, so the lighting truck empties before the backline truck pulls in, and nothing goes up on stage while the dock is still moving through it.

Dock
Lighting truck in: bars, fixtures, cable, 60 minutes.
Backline truck in the moment the lighting truck is empty: 45 minutes.
Clear the dock and get the empties out; 15 minutes.

Lighting
Rig the bars as soon as the lighting truck is off the dock: 45 minutes on stage.
Focus from the desk once the rig is up: 60 minutes.
Build the cues after focus: 30 minutes if the plot is clean, up to 90 if it is not.
Strike the rig when the show is down: 60 minutes.

PA
Fly the PA as soon as the lighting truck is off the dock: 75 minutes.
Ring out the house: 20 minutes.

Monitors
Set monitor world once the backline truck is off the dock: 45 minutes.
Ring out the wedges: 20 minutes.

Band
Backline up as soon as the dock is clear of the second truck: 45 minutes on stage.
Soundcheck when the house and the wedges are both rung out: 60 minutes, drums first.
Band dinner after soundcheck: 60 minutes in the green room.

House
Set front of house from two hours in: 60 minutes, merch, bars, ushers.
Clean the house after the band go to dinner; 30 minutes.
Doors when the house manager calls them; 30 minutes of walk-up.
Show on stage once the house is in, and it runs as long as it runs.
Backline out fifteen minutes after the show is down: 45 minutes on the dock.

Notes
The dock is the first bottleneck and the stage is the second. Focus and cue-build both want the desk, so they are strictly sequential. Soundcheck is the only step in the day that waits on two separate departments at once.
>>>

<<<
Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn, 90 guests

The ceremony breaks at four o'clock and this sheet starts there. One kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one band. The planner owns the room call; the MC owns everything that goes through the microphone. Nothing on the pass overlaps: the kitchen plates one course at a time and the floor waits for it.

Room
Flip the ceremony room to reception seating: 45 minutes, chairs out, rounds in, linen on.
Dress the tables with centrepieces, place cards and candles; 15 minutes once the flip is done.
Seat the guests when the planner calls the room; 15 minutes to get 90 people down.

Foyer
Open the bar as soon as the ceremony breaks; 20 minutes to set and pour the first round.
Pass canapes in the foyer from twenty minutes in, and keep passing for forty minutes to an hour, however long the photographs take.
Call the room to dinner once the canapes are done; 5 minutes.

Kitchen
Starters plate up fifteen minutes after the room starts seating; 15 minutes on the pass.
Mains go on the pass five minutes after the starter plates are cleared; 30 minutes.
Dessert plates up the moment the cake is cut; 15 minutes.

Floor
Serve the starters; 10 minutes.
Clear the starters twenty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the mains; 15 minutes.
Clear the mains forty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the dessert; 10 minutes.

Programme
Welcome toast as soon as the guests are seated; 5 minutes on the microphone.
First dance once the main plates are cleared; 5 minutes.
Speeches when the MC cues them: two or three of them, fifteen minutes total, twenty-five at the outside.
Cut the cake straight after the speeches; 10 minutes.
Dancing starts ten minutes after the dessert is served and runs until the band's last set.

Notes for the day
The photographs are the only thing we do not control, so the canape window is the slack in the sheet: if the couple are late back from the orchard the bar carries it. Everything downstream of the room call is fixed. If the speeches run long, the kitchen holds the dessert rather than plating it early — the pass is the bottleneck and a plated dessert sitting under a lamp is worse than a five minute gap on the floor.
>>>

<<<
HIIT Circuit Card — three athletes, four stations

Small group session, forty-five minutes on the clock including the warm-up and the stretch. There is one rower, one kettlebell, one box and one sled in the corner of the gym, and three of you. That means one station sits empty every round, and it means nobody ever waits on equipment if the rotation is respected.

The rule
Sixty seconds of work, all out, then sixty seconds of rest. Nobody starts a station until the athlete ahead of them has left it. If you are early, stand at the station and breathe; do not start.

Warm-up
Five minutes on the floor together: skipping, hip openers, shoulder pass-throughs, two sets of ten air squats. All three of you start at the same time and finish at the same time.

The stations
Rower: damper on five, pull hard, do not chase the split on the last ten seconds.
Kettlebell swings: one bell, hips not arms, chest tall at the top.
Box step-overs: alternate the lead leg, full extension at the top, no rebound.
Sled push: the length of the turf and back, low hands, short steps.

The rotation
Round 1: A on the rower, B on the kettlebell, C on the box.
Round 2: A on the kettlebell, B on the box, C on the sled.
Round 3: A on the box, B on the sled, C on the rower.
Round 4: A on the sled, B on the rower, C on the kettlebell.

Rest
Sixty seconds of rest on the floor after every station. Walk it off, do not sit down, do not lean on the next piece of equipment while somebody is still using it. There is no rest after the fourth station: that one runs straight into the cooldown.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor when all three of you have finished the fourth station: easy bike or a walk, then quads, hips and thoracic spine. Nobody leaves early; the cooldown starts together.

Coach's note
The sled is the one that wrecks the rotation if somebody drags it. It is the longest reset and it is at the far end of the turf, so the athlete coming off the sled is the one most likely to hold up the person behind them. Watch that hand-off.
>>>

<<<
Partner Upper-Body Superset Session

Two lifters, one flat bench with a barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar and two rowing ergs. The whole session should take about 25 minutes. You work as a pair: while Partner A is on the first exercise of a superset, Partner B is on the second, and then you swap; nobody waits for equipment if you keep the order.

Warm-up
Both partners start together with 5 minutes of easy rowing on the ergs, followed by 3 minutes of arm circles and band pull-aparts.

Superset A: bench press and dumbbell row (2 rounds)
Partner A loads the bar and does a set of 8 bench presses, which takes about 40 seconds. Partner B starts on the dumbbell row at the same time, 8 per side, also about 40 seconds. Then swap: A goes to the rows once B has finished with the dumbbells, and B takes the bench as soon as A racks the bar. After both exercises, rest 90 seconds before the next round. Do 2 rounds, resting after each.

Superset B: overhead press and pull-ups (2 rounds)
Move straight on after the last rest. Partner A does 8 strict overhead presses with the dumbbells, about 45 seconds, while Partner B does a set of pull-ups, 6 to 10 reps, about 30 seconds. Swap when both are done: A moves to the pull-up bar, and B takes the dumbbells when A sets them down. Rest 2 minutes between rounds; there is no rest after the second round.

Cool-down
Finish together with 5 minutes of stretching: doorway chest stretch, lat stretch on the pull-up bar, and slow shoulder rolls.
>>>

<<<
Partner Upper-Body Superset Session

Two lifters, one flat bench with a barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar and two rowing ergs. The whole session should take about 25 minutes. You work as a pair: while Partner A is on the first exercise of a superset, Partner B is on the second, and then you swap; nobody waits for equipment if you keep the order.

Warm-up
Both partners start together with 5 minutes of easy rowing on the ergs, followed by 3 minutes of arm circles and band pull-aparts.

Superset A: bench press and dumbbell row (2 rounds)
Partner A loads the bar and does a set of 8 bench presses, which takes about 40 seconds. Partner B starts on the dumbbell row at the same time, 8 per side, also about 40 seconds. Then swap: A goes to the rows once B has finished with the dumbbells, and B takes the bench as soon as A racks the bar. After both exercises, rest 90 seconds before the next round. Do 2 rounds, resting after each.

Superset B: overhead press and pull-ups (2 rounds)
Move straight on after the last rest. Partner A does 8 strict overhead presses with the dumbbells, about 45 seconds, while Partner B does a set of pull-ups, 6 to 10 reps, about 30 seconds. Swap when both are done: A moves to the pull-up bar, and B takes the dumbbells when A sets them down. Rest 2 minutes between rounds; there is no rest after the second round.

Cool-down
Finish together with 5 minutes of stretching: doorway chest stretch, lat stretch on the pull-up bar, and slow shoulder rolls.
>>>

<<<
Erg Session — four rowers, two machines

Two ergs in the bay and four of us, so we row in pairs and the pair that is off the machines is the pair that is resting. A and B are the first pair, C and D the second. Nobody sits on a machine they are not rowing.

Warm-up
A and B warm up first: 10 minutes, rate 18, light pressure, half slide to full slide.
C and D come in ten minutes later and take the machines for their own 10 minute warm-up.

The pieces
Three pieces, four minutes each, rate 26 to 28, target split on the monitor.
A and B take the first piece as soon as C and D are off the machines.
C and D take the first piece straight off the back of A and B's first piece.
A and B start their second piece four minutes after their first one ends.
C and D take the second piece as soon as A and B are off.
A and B start their third piece four minutes after their second one ends.
C and D take the third piece as soon as A and B are off.

Technique drill
Three minutes each, one at a time, coach on the machine with you: pause at the finish, pause at half slide, then build. A goes first once C and D are off the last piece, then B, then C, then D.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor together once the last drill is done: legs up the wall, hips, lats, then a cup of tea.

Coach
Brief the crew on the boards before anyone gets on: 5 minutes.
Call splits from the first piece: 20 minutes on the clock, watch the catch not the monitor.
Run the drills: 12 minutes, one rower at a time, straight through.
Debrief after the cooldown: 10 minutes, what the splits said and what Saturday looks like.

Note
The rests are not steps for the first pair: they are the gap between one piece ending and the next one starting, because the machines are handed over in that gap and the second pair is using them. The second pair's rests are the first pair's pieces. That is the whole design of the session.
>>>

<<<
Practice Plan — Thursday AM, three lanes

We have three lanes for two and a half hours and one set of starting blocks. Lane 1 is the sprint group, lane 2 the middle distance, lane 3 the distance group. Everything except the sprint set runs in all three lanes at once; the sprint set runs one lane at a time off the blocks, so lanes wait their turn.

On deck
Brief the squad on the pool deck: what the morning is, who is in which lane, 5 minutes.
Watch the warm-up from the deck and fix anything ugly; 15 minutes.

Warm-up
All three lanes start together: 20 minutes, 800 easy, mixed stroke, breathing every five on the last hundred.

Whiteboard
Call the lanes to the wall when the warm-up is done and walk the main set on the whiteboard; 5 minutes. Nobody pushes off until the board is done.

Kick set
20 minutes of kick, boards for lanes 1 and 2, vertical kick for lane 3, once the whiteboard talk is over.

Main set
Lane 1: 30 to 50 minutes, 40 minutes is the plan.
Lane 2: 30 to 50 minutes, 45 minutes is the plan.
Lane 3: 30 to 50 minutes, 50 minutes is the plan.
Every lane swims its own main set and the sprint set does not start until the last lane is in.

Sprint set
One set of blocks, one lane at a time, 10 minutes each.
Lane 1 goes first, off the blocks, dive starts, 25s flat out.
Lane 2 goes second, same thing, on the lane 1 group's last dive.
Lane 3 goes third and gets the extra rest it will need.
Time the sprints from the deck: 30 minutes, stopwatch and the wall clock.

Cooldown
All three lanes cool down together once the last sprint is in: 10 minutes, 300 easy backstroke and breaststroke.

Debrief
10 minutes on the deck at the end: splits, what to fix, Saturday's meet.

Note
The main set is the only place a lane can run long and the only place the plan gives them room to. Everything after it is a join: the blocks cannot be shared and the cooldown starts together or it does not start at all.
>>>

<<<
Backyard Barbecue: Smoker and Grill

Two cooks, one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner and a cooler for holding. The pork owns the smoker all day; everything else happens in the last two hours.

Pork shoulder
Light the smoker and bring it to 250°F; 45 minutes. While it comes up, trim the shoulder and rub it heavily with salt, pepper and paprika; 25 minutes. Put the shoulder on once the smoker holds temperature and smoke it unwrapped for 6 hours, until the bark is dark and set. Wrap it tightly in butcher paper; 10 minutes. Back on the smoker, wrapped, until the thickest part probes soft — usually another 3 hours, sometimes four. Hold it wrapped in a cooler for one to three hours; it will not get cold and it only gets better. Pull the meat by hand; 30 minutes.

Beans
When the pork goes into the cooler, fry the bacon and onion in the pot on the side burner for 12 minutes, then add the beans, molasses and a ladle of drippings and let them tick over on the lowest flame until you serve.

Slaw
Start the slaw at the same time. Shred the cabbage and carrot; 20 minutes. Whisk the buttermilk dressing; 8 minutes. Dress the slaw and put it in the refrigerator for at least 45 minutes so the cabbage softens.

Grill
Light the kettle an hour before you eat; 25 minutes to a clean bed of coals. Grill the sausages for 14 minutes. Grill the corn for 10 minutes. Toast the buns for 3 minutes, last, so they stay warm.

Table
Set out plates, pickles and sauce once the buns are off; 10 minutes. Call everyone over when both cooks say it is ready; 5 minutes to lay it all out.
>>>

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Country Loaf: Two Boules, One Dutch Oven

One batch of dough, two loaves, and a single dutch oven that has to bake them one after the other. One oven, one baker, one refrigerator. Times count from eight in the morning; the loaves come out of the fridge the next day.

Levain
Mix 50 g of ripe starter with 100 g of flour and 100 g of water in a jar; 5 minutes. Leave the jar at room temperature until it domes and smells sweet, 4 to 6 hours.

Dough
Weigh the flour, water and salt for the whole bake first thing; 10 minutes. At half past eight, whisk 900 g of flour into 680 g of water; 5 minutes. Let it autolyse for 1 hour. When the levain is ripe, squeeze it into the autolysed dough with 20 g of salt and work it by hand for 10 minutes. Bulk ferment at 24°C until the dough has risen by half, 3 to 5 hours. Fold the dough in the bowl half an hour after mixing, again half an hour later, and a third time after another half hour; each fold takes 2 minutes.

Divide and shape
Tip the dough out, cut it in two and preshape each piece into a loose round; 10 minutes. Let the rounds rest on the bench for 25 minutes. Shape both boules tightly and settle them into floured bannetons; 10 minutes. Retard them in the refrigerator, 10 to 14 hours.

Bake
Three quarters of an hour before the dough comes out, put the dutch oven in the oven and heat both to 250°C. Score the first loaf and lower it in; 3 minutes. Bake the first loaf covered for 20 minutes, then uncover it and bake for another 20 minutes until the crust is dark. Cool it on a rack for at least an hour before cutting. Re-heat the empty dutch oven for 10 minutes. Score the second loaf and lower it in; 3 minutes. Bake the second loaf covered for 20 minutes, then uncover it for a final 20 minutes. Cool the second loaf on the rack beside the first.
>>>

<<<
Breakfast for Six on One Griddle

One electric griddle, a two-slice toaster, a burr grinder, a drip coffee maker and an oven turned to its lowest setting to hold things warm. One cook, six people, everyone eating at nine.

Prep
Whisk the dry pancake ingredients together, then beat in the buttermilk and eggs; 10 minutes. Let the batter stand for 20 minutes while the griddle does its first job. Crack a dozen eggs into a jug and season them; 5 minutes. Set the table and lay out six places; 10 minutes. Put six plates in the oven at its lowest setting and leave them there until you call everyone.

Griddle
Everything cooks on the one griddle, in order. Heat the griddle to 375°F; 8 minutes. Lay the bacon out and cook it for 14 minutes, turning once, then move it to the warm oven. Scrape the griddle and wipe off the fat; 3 minutes. Pancakes go on as soon as the griddle is clean and the batter has rested, in three passes: the first pass takes 6 minutes, the second another 6, and the third 6 more. Slide each pass into the oven as it comes off. Drop the griddle to 300°F and give it 4 minutes to settle, then scramble the eggs slowly for 7 minutes.

Toast
The toaster takes two slices at a time. Start the first batch of toast when the last pancake pass goes on; 3 minutes. Run a second batch straight after; 3 minutes. Butter all of it; 4 minutes.

Coffee
Start the grinder ten minutes after the bacon goes on so the pot is fresh. Grind the beans; 2 minutes. Brew a full pot; 9 minutes.

Serve
Call everyone when the eggs, the toast and the coffee are all ready, and carry the warm plates through; 5 minutes.
>>>

<<<
Holiday Cookie Batch: Three Doughs, One Oven

Three doughs, one stand mixer, one oven and two sheet pans. A pan has to cool before it is reloaded or the next batch spreads, so the oven waits on the pans as often as the pans wait on the oven. One baker, one afternoon, everything boxed by evening.

Doughs
Cream the butter and sugar for the sugar cookies and beat in the flour; 12 minutes in the mixer. Wrap the dough and chill it for 1 hour.
Wash the bowl, then make the chocolate chip dough the same way; 12 minutes. That one goes straight onto a pan.
Wash the bowl again and make the gingerbread dough with molasses and spice; 15 minutes. Chill it for 2 hours.

Order
The oven runs one pan at a time, in this order: chocolate chip, sugar, gingerbread. Nothing goes in until its dough is cut and a cool pan is free.

Baking
Heat the oven to 350°F; 15 minutes. Scoop the chocolate chip dough onto the first pan; 6 minutes. Bake it for 11 minutes. Slide the pan onto a rack and let it cool for 12 minutes before you touch the cookies, and let the pan itself cool for 20 minutes before it goes back in.

Roll and cut the chilled sugar cookies onto the second pan; 14 minutes. Bake for 9 minutes as soon as the chocolate chip pan is out. Let the sugar cookies cool on the rack for 10 minutes; the second pan needs its own 20 minutes before anything else touches it.

Roll the gingerbread a quarter inch thick and cut it out; 18 minutes. Bake for 10 minutes once the sugar cookies are out and the first pan has cooled. Cool the gingerbread for 15 minutes. Ice the gingerbread when it is cold; 25 minutes.

Box everything; 10 minutes.
>>>

Weekday Lentil Soup and Salad for Four

Lunch at half past twelve. One cook, two burners, one toaster oven, one stick blender. Nothing here is fussy; the only real constraint is that the cook can stand in one place at a time, so the salad and the bread wait until the soup is quietly simmering.

Soup

Bread
Cut the loaf into thick slices once the soup is simmering; 3 minutes. Warm them in the toaster oven for 8 minutes. Wrap the warm bread in a cloth and leave it on the table.

Table
Lay four places once the bread is wrapped; 5 minutes. When the soup, the salad and the bread are all ready, carry the pot and the bowl through together; 3 minutes.
>>>

<<<
Thanksgiving for Eight with One Oven

We eat at six o'clock sharp. There is one oven and four burners, and two of you in the kitchen, so the oven schedule decides everything else. The turkey owns the oven for most of the afternoon; the sides go in while it rests, one after another.

The turkey (14 pounds)
Take the turkey out of the refrigerator 40 minutes before you season it so it is not fridge-cold. Heat the oven to 325°F; give it 20 minutes to come up. Pat the bird dry, rub it all over with softened butter, salt and pepper, and tuck halved onions and thyme into the cavity; this takes about twenty minutes. Roast the turkey for 3 hours, until a thermometer in the thigh reads 165°F. Move the turkey to a carving board and let it rest, loosely tented with foil, for 40 minutes before carving. Carving takes about 15 minutes.

Gravy
As soon as the turkey comes out, pour the pan drippings into a saucepan, whisk in flour and cook for 3 minutes, then whisk in stock and simmer the gravy for 10 minutes until it coats a spoon. Keep it warm over the lowest flame until dinner.

Stuffing
Cut a loaf of day-old bread into cubes and spread them on a sheet pan; you can do this first thing. Twenty minutes before the turkey is due out, melt butter in a skillet and cook diced onion and celery for 10 minutes until soft. Toss the bread with the vegetables, sage and two cups of stock and turn it into a buttered dish; 10 minutes. Bake the stuffing at 375°F for 35 minutes the moment the turkey is out; the oven will already be hot.

Green bean casserole
About ten minutes after the turkey comes out, trim two pounds of green beans and blanch them for 4 minutes in salted boiling water, then drain. Make the mushroom sauce: cook sliced mushrooms in butter for 8 minutes, add cream and simmer for 5 minutes. Combine the beans and sauce in a baking dish and scatter fried onions on top; 5 minutes. Bake the casserole for 20 minutes as soon as the stuffing comes out.

Mashed potatoes
When the turkey comes out, peel and quarter four pounds of potatoes, about 15 minutes, cover with cold salted water and boil for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain, then mash with warm cream and a stick of butter; give it 10 minutes. Hold the potatoes covered on the back burner until everything else is ready.

Dinner rolls
The rolls only need warming: slide them into the oven for 8 minutes right after the casserole comes out.

Serve
Carry everything to the table together.
>>>

<<<
Three-Course Dinner for Six: Two Burners, One Oven

Guests sit down at half past seven. There are two burners, one oven and one cook, so the oven does the braise first and the tart second, and the burners are rarely both free.

Mise en place
Chop the mirepoix, trim the short ribs and measure the stock: forty minutes of knife work before anything goes on the heat.

Main: braised short ribs
Heat the oven to 300°F; give it 20 minutes. Sear the short ribs in a heavy pot over high heat for 12 minutes, turning once. Lift the ribs out, soften the mirepoix in the same pot for 8 minutes, add the wine and reduce it for 5 minutes, then return the ribs with the stock. Braise the ribs, covered, for 3 hours. Rest the pot off the heat for 20 minutes, then skim the fat and reduce the braising liquid for 15 minutes.

Starter: leek and potato soup
Two hours into the braise, sweat the sliced leeks in butter for 10 minutes. Add the potatoes and the stock and simmer for 30 minutes, then blend the soup smooth; 5 minutes. Hold it warm on the back burner until the guests are seated.

Dessert: apple tart
Roll the pastry and line the tin; 15 minutes. Chill the shell in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes and no more than two hours. Slice the apples and arrange them in the shell; 20 minutes. Bake the tart for 45 minutes the moment the ribs leave the oven, while the ribs are resting.

Service
Ladle the soup when everyone is seated; ten minutes at the table. Plate the ribs ten minutes after the soup bowls are cleared, and give the plating five minutes. Let the main course run as long as it runs. The tart goes out twenty minutes after the main plates come back; ten minutes to slice and serve.
>>>

Saturday Brunch for Four

Everything on the table at ten. The bacon cooks in the oven so the stove is free for pancakes; the fruit salad and the coffee fill the gaps. One person can do this in about 45 minutes.

Bacon
Lay a pound of bacon on a rack over a sheet pan and bake at 400°F for 20 minutes, until crisp, turning the pan once halfway. Drain on paper towels for 2 minutes; it stays warm for a while.

Pancakes
Whisk together two cups of flour, two tablespoons of sugar, a tablespoon of baking powder and a teaspoon of salt; 5 minutes. In a jug beat two eggs with a cup and a half of milk and three tablespoons of melted butter, then stir the wet into the dry until just combined, another 5 minutes; lumps are fine. Let the batter rest for 10 minutes while the bacon cooks. Heat a griddle over medium heat for 5 minutes. Cook the pancakes in batches, a quarter cup each, about 2 minutes per side, 15 minutes for the whole batch.

Fruit salad
Halve a pint of strawberries, cube a small melon and a mango, and add a cup of blueberries; this takes about 10 minutes. Squeeze half a lime over the top and chill for at least 15 minutes.

Coffee
Grind the beans and set up the pot, 3 minutes, then brew a full pot, which takes 8 minutes, timed to finish as the pancakes come off the griddle.

Serve
Bring everything out together while the pancakes are hot; 2 minutes.
>>>

Weeknight Chicken and Broccoli Stir-Fry with Rice

Serves two. You have two burners and about 35 minutes, and one person cooking. Rice goes on first because it takes the longest; the stir-fry is quick and should go from wok to plate in under a minute.

Rice
Rinse one cup of jasmine rice until the water runs clear, about 2 minutes. Put it in a small pot with one and a quarter cups of water and bring to a boil over high heat, about 5 minutes. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and let it steam, lid on, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork just before serving; 1 minute.

Prep
While the rice comes to a boil, slice a pound of chicken thighs into thin strips, about 5 minutes. Toss the strips with a tablespoon of soy sauce and a teaspoon of cornstarch and let them sit for 10 minutes. While the chicken marinates, cut a head of broccoli into small florets and mince three cloves of garlic and a thumb of ginger; 5 minutes. Stir together the sauce in a small bowl: two tablespoons of soy sauce, one of oyster sauce, a teaspoon of sugar and a splash of rice vinegar; 2 minutes.

Stir-fry
When the rice comes off the heat to steam, heat a wok over the highest flame until it smokes, about 3 minutes. Add oil and the chicken and stir-fry for 4 minutes until browned; remove to a plate. Add the broccoli with a splash of water, cover, and steam for 3 minutes. Uncover, add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds, then return the chicken, pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until glossy.

Serve immediately over the rice.
>>>

<<<
Passaging Two Flasks of Adherent HEK293 Cells

Two T75 flasks at about 90 % confluence are split 1:6 into four new flasks. The room has one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge and one microscope with a haemocytometer. Only one flask can be open in the cabinet at a time, so the two flasks queue for it while the centrifuge and the microscope stay free. Work with pre-warmed medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA throughout; nothing cold touches the cells. One operator.

Preparation
1. Wipe down the cabinet, lay out pipettes and tubes, and let the blower run; 10 minutes.
2. Check both flasks on the microscope for confluence and contamination; 10 minutes.

Flask A
3. Aspirate the spent medium and rinse the monolayer with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes in the cabinet.
4. Add 2 mL of trypsin-EDTA, rock the flask and return it to the incubator for 5 minutes.
5. Knock the flask, check detachment and neutralise with 8 mL of medium; 5 minutes in the cabinet.
6. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube and spin at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
7. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
8. Count the cells on the haemocytometer; 6 minutes.
9. Seed two new T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes in the cabinet.
10. Return the new flasks to the incubator and leave them to settle overnight, at least 16 hours.

Flask B
11. Start flask B the moment flask A leaves the cabinet: aspirate and rinse with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes.
12. Trypsinise flask B in the incubator for 5 minutes.
13. Neutralise flask B as soon as flask A is out of the cabinet again; 5 minutes.
14. Spin flask B at 300 × g for 5 minutes once the centrifuge is free.
15. Resuspend the flask B pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
16. Count flask B on the haemocytometer once flask A has been counted; 6 minutes.
17. Seed two more T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes.
18. Return them to the incubator to settle overnight alongside the first pair.

Finishing
19. Wipe the cabinet down, discard the waste and switch the blower to standby; 10 minutes.
20. Write the passage number, the split ratio and the counts into the culture log; 5 minutes.
>>>

Passaging Two Flasks of Adherent HEK293 Cells

Two T75 flasks at about 90 % confluence are split 1:6 into four new flasks. The room has one biosafety cabinet, one 37 °C water bath, one CO₂ incubator, one benchtop centrifuge and one microscope with a haemocytometer. Only one flask can be open in the cabinet at a time, so the two flasks queue for it while the centrifuge and the microscope stay free. Work with pre-warmed medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA throughout; nothing cold touches the cells. One operator.

Preparation
1. Wipe down the cabinet, lay out pipettes and tubes, and let the blower run; 10 minutes.
2. Check both flasks on the microscope for confluence and contamination; 10 minutes.

Flask A
3. Aspirate the spent medium and rinse the monolayer with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes in the cabinet.
4. Add 2 mL of trypsin-EDTA, rock the flask and return it to the incubator for 5 minutes.
5. Knock the flask, check detachment and neutralise with 8 mL of medium; 5 minutes in the cabinet.
6. Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube and spin at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
7. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
8. Count the cells on the haemocytometer; 6 minutes.
9. Seed two new T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes in the cabinet.
10. Return the new flasks to the incubator and leave them to settle overnight, at least 16 hours.

Flask B
11. Start flask B the moment flask A leaves the cabinet: aspirate and rinse with 5 mL of PBS; 4 minutes.
12. Trypsinise flask B in the incubator for 5 minutes.
13. Neutralise flask B as soon as flask A is out of the cabinet again; 5 minutes.
14. Spin flask B at 300 × g for 5 minutes once the centrifuge is free.
15. Resuspend the flask B pellet in 10 mL of fresh medium; 4 minutes.
16. Count flask B on the haemocytometer once flask A has been counted; 6 minutes.
17. Seed two more T75 flasks at 1:6 and label them; 6 minutes.
18. Return them to the incubator to settle overnight alongside the first pair.

Finishing
19. Wipe the cabinet down, discard the waste and switch the blower to standby; 10 minutes.
20. Write the passage number, the split ratio and the counts into the culture log; 5 minutes.
>>>

Sandwich ELISA on Two Plates, One Washer

Two 96-well plates are run half an hour apart through a sandwich ELISA for a secreted cytokine. There is one automated plate washer, one 37 °C plate incubator that holds two plates, one plate reader and one operator. The washer is the bottleneck: no two plates can be in it at once, and every incubation is bracketed by a wash.

Day 1
1. Coat plate 1 with 100 µL per well of capture antibody in carbonate buffer, seal it and leave it in the cold room at 4 °C overnight. Take it out when you are ready to start, not before.
2. Coat plate 2 the same way half an hour later, so the two plates stay half an hour apart all day.

Day 2, reagents
3. Fifteen hours into the coat, make up the seven-point standard curve in assay diluent; 30 minutes.
4. Dilute the samples 1:4 into assay diluent and lay out the plate map; 30 minutes.

Day 2, plate 1
5. Wash the plate four times with 300 µL of wash buffer; 5 minutes on the washer.
6. Block with 200 µL per well of assay diluent for 1 hour at 37 °C.
7. Wash four times; 5 minutes on the washer.
8. Add 100 µL of standards and samples and incubate for 2 hours at 37 °C. Nothing goes on the plate until the dilutions are laid out.
9. Wash four times; 5 minutes on the washer.
10. Add 100 µL of biotinylated detection antibody and incubate for 1 hour at 37 °C.
11. Wash four times; 5 minutes on the washer.
12. Add 100 µL of TMB substrate, develop in the dark for exactly 15 minutes and stop with 50 µL of 2 N sulfuric acid.
13. Read the absorbance at 450 nm with a 570 nm reference; 5 minutes on the reader.

Day 2, plate 2
14. Wash plate 2 four times as soon as the washer is free; 5 minutes.
15. Block plate 2 with 200 µL of assay diluent for 1 hour at 37 °C.
16. Wash plate 2 again once plate 1 is off the washer; 5 minutes.
17. Add the standards and samples to plate 2 and incubate for 2 hours at 37 °C.
18. Wash plate 2; 5 minutes.
19. Add the detection antibody to plate 2 and incubate for 1 hour at 37 °C.
20. Wash plate 2 a final time; 5 minutes.
21. Develop plate 2 with TMB for exactly 15 minutes and stop it.
22. Read plate 2 at 450 nm; 5 minutes.
>>>

Streaking Three Cultures onto Selective Media

Three overnight broths are streaked for single colonies on selective agar, incubated at 37 °C and read the next morning. The bench has one Bunsen burner with a single loop station, one 37 °C incubator with room for two plates on the free shelf, one staining rack and one microscope. One technician works the bench; a supervisor reads the plates before anything is subcultured.

Setup
1. Wipe the bench with 70 % ethanol and light the burner; 10 minutes.
2. Label three selective plates with the isolate number, the medium and the date; 10 minutes.

Streaking
3. Streak isolate 1 for single colonies in four quadrants, flaming the loop between each; 10 minutes.
4. Streak isolate 2 the same way; 10 minutes.
5. Streak isolate 3 the same way; 10 minutes.
6. Invert plates 1 and 2 and put them on the incubator shelf overnight, 16 to 20 hours.
7. Only two plates fit on the shelf, so hold plate 3 at room temperature on the bench until plate 1 comes out.
8. Incubate plate 3 at 37 °C for 6 hours once the shelf is free.

Reading
9. Read plate 1 in the morning: count the colonies, note the colour and record the selective growth; 15 minutes.
10. Read plate 2 the same way; 15 minutes.
11. Read plate 3 at the end of its run; 15 minutes.

Subculture and stain
12. Pick a single well-separated colony from each of plates 1 and 2 into fresh broth; 10 minutes at the loop station.
13. Do not streak the purity plate until the supervisor has signed off the readings. Streaking it takes 15 minutes.
14. Incubate the purity plate at 37 °C for 8 hours.
15. Make a smear from the picked colony and heat-fix it; 10 minutes.
16. Gram stain the smear on the rack: crystal violet, iodine, decolourise, safranin; 15 minutes.
17. Read the stain under oil immersion and record the morphology; 15 minutes.
>>>

<<<
Colony PCR Screen with a Diagnostic Gel

Eight candidate clones are screened by PCR and the products are run on a single agarose gel. The bench has one thermocycler, one microcentrifuge, a microwave, one gel rig and one transilluminator, and one person runs the whole thing. The cycling block is long enough to cast and set the gel while it runs, so start the agarose partway through the run rather than waiting for the machine to finish.

Part 1: Reaction setup
1. Thaw the primers, dNTPs and 10× buffer on ice; 15 minutes. Keep the polymerase in the cold block until the last moment.
2. Assemble a 25 µL master mix on ice for eight reactions plus one spare; 10 minutes of pipetting.
3. Aliquot 25 µL into eight strip tubes, add 1 µL of each colony suspension and spin them down for 30 seconds in the microcentrifuge; 5 minutes.

Part 2: Cycling
4. Load the strip tubes into the thermocycler and start the program; 3 minutes.
5. Run 95 °C for 3 minutes, then 35 cycles of 95 °C for 30 seconds, 58 °C for 30 seconds and 72 °C for 45 seconds, then a final 72 °C for 5 minutes. The block reports 1 hour 50 minutes.

Part 3: Agarose gel
6. Twenty-five minutes into the cycling run, weigh 1.0 g of agarose into 100 mL of 1× TAE and microwave for 3 minutes, swirling once, until no lens of undissolved agarose is left.
7. Cool the flask on the bench for 12 minutes, until it is comfortable to hold.
8. Add 5 µL of DNA stain, pour the gel into the casting tray and seat the 10-well comb; 3 minutes.
9. Let the gel set for 35 minutes at room temperature. Do not rush this; a soft gel tears at the wells.
10. Remove the comb and place the gel in the rig under 1× TAE; 2 minutes.

Part 4: Run and read
11. Ten minutes after the gel is poured to set, thaw the 100 bp ladder and mix it with 6× loading dye; 5 minutes.
12. When the cycling finishes, spin the tubes down and add 5 µL of loading dye to each; 5 minutes.
13. Load 10 µL per well alongside 5 µL of ladder; 8 minutes. Nothing goes into a well until the gel is in the rig and the ladder is ready.
14. Run the gel at 120 V for 40 minutes, until the dye front is two-thirds down.
15. Image the gel on the transilluminator; 5 minutes.
16. Record which clones carry the insert and mark the plate; 10 minutes.
>>>

Plasmid Miniprep, Restriction Digest and Gel Check

This protocol takes a 5 mL overnight culture of E. coli carrying a pUC-based plasmid through a spin-column miniprep, a diagnostic double digest, and an agarose gel. The bench has one benchtop centrifuge, one microcentrifuge, one 37 °C heat block, one 65 °C heat block, a microwave, one spectrophotometer and a single gel rig, so plan the shared equipment: the gel can be cast while the culture is spinning down, and the ladder can be prepared during the digest. One person runs the whole protocol.

Part 1: Miniprep
1. Pellet the culture: transfer 5 mL of the overnight culture to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 4,000 × g for 10 minutes. Discard the supernatant.
2. Resuspend the pellet in 250 µL of Resuspension Buffer (with RNase A) by vortexing; about 2 minutes.
3. Add 250 µL of Lysis Buffer, invert gently 6 times and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes. Do not exceed 5 minutes.
4. Add 350 µL of Neutralization Buffer, invert 6 times, and centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 minutes in the microcentrifuge.
5. Load the cleared lysate onto a spin column and spin for 1 minute. Discard the flow-through.
6. Wash the column with 700 µL of Wash Buffer, spin for 1 minute, discard the flow-through, then spin the empty column for 2 minutes to dry the membrane.
7. Transfer the column to a clean tube, add 50 µL of Elution Buffer, wait 1 minute, and spin for 1 minute to elute.
8. Measure the concentration on the spectrophotometer; 3 minutes.

Part 2: Agarose gel
9. While the culture is pelleting, weigh 0.5 g of agarose into 50 mL of 1× TAE and microwave for 2 minutes, swirling once, until fully dissolved.
10. Cool the flask on the bench for 10 minutes, then add 5 µL of DNA stain and pour the gel into the casting tray with the comb in place; 2 minutes.
11. Let the gel set for 30 minutes at room temperature, then remove the comb and place the gel in the rig under 1× TAE; 2 minutes.

Part 3: Digest
12. In a 0.2 mL tube combine 500 ng of plasmid, 2 µL of 10× buffer, 0.5 µL each of EcoRI and HindIII, and water to 20 µL; 5 minutes of pipetting.
13. Incubate at 37 °C for 60 minutes in the heat block.
14. Heat-inactivate the enzymes at 65 °C for 20 minutes.
15. Ten minutes into the digest, thaw the 1 kb ladder and mix 4 µL of 6× loading dye into a fresh tube for each lane; 5 minutes.
16. Add loading dye to the digest, briefly spin down the tube in the microcentrifuge for 30 seconds, and load 10 µL per well alongside 5 µL of ladder; 5 minutes.
17. Run the gel at 100 V for 45 minutes, until the dye front is two-thirds down the gel.
18. Image the gel on the transilluminator and record band sizes; 5 minutes.
>>>

Western Blot: SDS-PAGE, Wet Transfer and Overnight Primary

One 10-well precast gel is run, wet-transferred to PVDF and probed overnight. The bench has one gel tank, one wet transfer tank, one orbital rocker that takes a single tray, a heat block, a microcentrifuge, a cold room and one chemiluminescence imager. The transfer tank and the rocker are the two things nothing else can share, so the blot moves through them one stage at a time.

Sample preparation
1. Thaw the lysates on ice and normalise them to 2 mg/mL; 15 minutes.
2. Add 4× Laemmli buffer and denature at 95 °C for 5 minutes in the heat block.
3. Spin the tubes for 2 minutes in the microcentrifuge to collect condensate.

Gel
4. Assemble the tank, seat the precast gel and fill with running buffer; 10 minutes.
5. Load 20 µg per lane and 5 µL of protein ladder; 10 minutes. Nothing is loaded until the denatured samples have been spun down.
6. Run at 120 V for 75 minutes, until the dye front reaches the foot of the gel.

Transfer preparation
7. Put a litre of transfer buffer in the cold room an hour before you need it.
8. One hour into the run, wet a PVDF membrane in methanol for 30 seconds and equilibrate it in transfer buffer; 5 minutes.
9. Soak the fibre pads and filter paper in cold transfer buffer; 10 minutes.

Blot
10. Five minutes after the run ends, prise the gel out of the cassette and build the transfer sandwich with no bubbles; 10 minutes.
11. Transfer at 100 V for 60 minutes with an ice pack in the tank.
12. Stain the membrane with Ponceau S, photograph it and rinse it off; 10 minutes.
13. Block in 5 % milk on the rocker for 1 hour at room temperature.
14. Probe with primary antibody overnight in the cold room; 12 to 18 hours.
15. Wash three times for 10 minutes each on the rocker.
16. Probe with HRP-conjugated secondary on the rocker for 1 hour.

Western Blot: SDS-PAGE, Wet Transfer and Overnight Primary

One 10-well precast gel is run, wet-transferred to PVDF and probed overnight. The bench has one gel tank, one wet transfer tank, one orbital rocker that takes a single tray, a heat block, a microcentrifuge, a cold room and one chemiluminescence imager. The transfer tank and the rocker are the two things nothing else can share, so the blot moves through them one stage at a time.

Sample preparation
1. Thaw the lysates on ice and normalise them to 2 mg/mL; 15 minutes.
2. Add 4× Laemmli buffer and denature at 95 °C for 5 minutes in the heat block.
3. Spin the tubes for 2 minutes in the microcentrifuge to collect condensate.

Gel
4. Assemble the tank, seat the precast gel and fill with running buffer; 10 minutes.
5. Load 20 µg per lane and 5 µL of protein ladder; 10 minutes. Nothing is loaded until the denatured samples have been spun down.
6. Run at 120 V for 75 minutes, until the dye front reaches the foot of the gel.

Transfer preparation
7. Put a litre of transfer buffer in the cold room an hour before you need it.
8. One hour into the run, wet a PVDF membrane in methanol for 30 seconds and equilibrate it in transfer buffer; 5 minutes.
9. Soak the fibre pads and filter paper in cold transfer buffer; 10 minutes.

Blot
10. Five minutes after the run ends, prise the gel out of the cassette and build the transfer sandwich with no bubbles; 10 minutes.
11. Transfer at 100 V for 60 minutes with an ice pack in the tank.
12. Stain the membrane with Ponceau S, photograph it and rinse it off; 10 minutes.
13. Block in 5 % milk on the rocker for 1 hour at room temperature.
14. Probe with primary antibody overnight in the cold room; 12 to 18 hours.
15. Wash three times for 10 minutes each on the rocker.
16. Probe with HRP-conjugated secondary on the rocker for 1 hour.
17. Wash three times for 10 minutes each on the rocker.

Detection
18. Fifty minutes into the secondary, mix the ECL substrate; 5 minutes.
19. Drain the membrane, apply the substrate and let it work for 5 minutes.
20. Image the blot; 10 minutes of exposures.
21. Quantify the bands against the loading control; 15 minutes.
